title: DAILY RATION CARD — ORGANIC BBQ CRIX CHIPS
description: A laminated identification card issued by NutriCore Solutions LLC under federal emergency food rationing protocols. Stamped with a single day's allocation. The reverse side features a corporate logo and the slogan: 'Nutrition, Simplified.' Accompanying the card is a sealed foil bag, Organic BBQ Crix Chips, 42g net weight. Ingredients include processed cricket flour, artificial smoke flavoring, and seventeen stabilizers. The bag design is deliberately familiar. The contents are not.
intelligence:
Each additional degree Celsius of warming reduces global food production capacity by approximately 120 calories per person per day, roughly 4.4% of current daily consumption. Farmer adaptation offsets only about one-third of those losses.

  • Global crop yields could be 24% lower by 2100 under high-emissions scenarios
  • The US Midwest corn and soybean belt is among the hardest-hit regions
  • Even with adaptive measures such as new crop varieties, shifted planting schedules, the deficit is not recoverable
citation: Hultgren, Andrew, et al. "Climate Change Cuts Global Crop Yields, Even When Farmers Adapt." Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, 18 June 2025. https://sustainability.stanford.edu/news/climate-change-cuts-global-crop-yields-even-when-farmers-adapt

title: PERSONAL WATER FILTRATOR — AQUAVANCE MK.4
description: Handheld water purification device manufactured by AquaVance Corp under a federal emergency supply contract. The filter housing is cracked along one side and repaired with adhesive wrap. The internal membrane shows heavy discoloration from prolonged exposure to contaminated source water. A sticker on the base reads: 'For use with AquaVance Certified Water Sources only. Warranty void if used with municipal runoff, industrial grey water, or flood-origin supply.' The sticker has been scratched off. Most local water sources have dried up from long-term drought or are undrinkable from pollution. The few remaining sources are heavily regulated by government entities and licensed to private corporations. It was used with all of them.
intelligence:
Only 0.5% of all water on Earth is usable freshwater, and climate change is rapidly eroding even that.

  • Over 2 billion people currently lack access to safe drinking water
  • Half the world's population experiences severe water scarcity for at least part of the year
  • Terrestrial water storage has dropped at a rate of 1 cm per year over the past two decades
  • Flood-related disasters have surged by 134% since 2000 compared to the prior two decades
  • Droughts have increased by 29% in number and duration over the same period

Water-related disasters now account for 70% of all deaths caused by natural disasters globally.
citation: "Water and Climate Change." United Nations Climate Change, United Nations. https://www.un.org/en/climatechange/science/climate-issues/water

title: ASPHALT FRAGMENT — COASTAL ORIGIN
description: A section of road-grade asphalt, approximately 18cm across. The fracture pattern is consistent with long-term submersion and structural degradation from saltwater intrusion. A faded painted line, yellow in color, possibly a lane marking is still partially visible on the upper surface. Residents from such coastal regions have been forced to evacuate out of safety concerns as streets, infrastructure, and entire neighborhoods are reclaimed by rising water. Recovered from a coastal urban area. The city it came from is not named in the manifest. Based on aggregate composition, geological analysis places its origin somewhere along the California coast.
intelligence:
More than thirty years of satellite data confirm global sea level has risen approximately 9 centimeters since the early 1990s, closely matching 1990s projections, with one critical underestimation: ice sheet melt exceeded models by over 2 cm.

  • NASA confirmed in 2024 that the rate of rise has doubled over the 30-year monitoring period
  • Antarctic ice sheet destabilization is driven by warming ocean water eroding ice from below
  • Greenland ice flow has accelerated faster than projected
  • Sea level does not rise uniformly, low-lying US coastal areas face disproportionate exposure

Current projections now include the possibility of catastrophic ice-sheet collapse before the end of this century.
citation: Törnqvist, Torbjörn, and Sönke Dangendorf. "Satellites Confirm 1990s Sea-Level Predictions Were Shockingly Accurate." ScienceDaily, Tulane University, 6 Sept. 2025. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2025/09/250906013453.htm
Sea Level Rise and Coastal Flooding. Online video transcript, YouTube. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rdzsh8AETnM

title: FLAMME PRO 3 — CIVILIAN FIRE RETARDANT GRENADE
description: Consumer-grade fire retardant grenade manufactured by Flamme Defense Systems. The canister is scorched on one end and the safety pin has been pulled. Product description on the label reads: 'Ensures complete fire retardation in a 10ft radius. Protection of life and property from a safe distance. Flamme Launcher sold separately.'
intelligence:
Wildfires have more than doubled worldwide over the last 21 years. Fire seasons now start earlier in spring and extend later into autumn. Drier conditions driven by rising temperatures ignite dead vegetation at increasing rates.

  • Years where over 10 million acres burned in the US, once catastrophic, are now routine
  • Fires in wildland-urban interface areas release arsenic, lead, and volatile organic compounds from burning structures
  • Forty years ago, 5 million acres burned in a year would have been considered particularly bad. That figure now represents a mild season.
citation: Green, Fiona. "How and Why Wildfires Are Becoming More Common: Looking at the Past 10 Years of Wildfire Seasons in North America." Clarity Movement, 25 June 2025. https://www.clarity.io/blog/how-and-why-wildfires-are-becoming-more-common-looking-at-the-past-10-years-of-wildfire-seasons-in-north-america

title: PERSONAL COOLING VEST — COOLCORE RENTAL UNIT

CoolCore is not liable for heat-related illness sustained during use.' As temperatures regularly exceed survivable thresholds, personal cooling equipment has become a basic necessity managed and monetized by private contractors. The rental tag suggests it was returned. The condition of the interior lining suggests it was returned just in time.
intelligence:
2024 was the hottest year on record, with average temperatures exceeding 1.5°C above the pre-industrial baseline. The entire decade from 2015–2024 was the hottest ten-year period ever recorded.

  • Extreme heat events in US cities have risen from 2 per year in the 1960s to 10 per year between 2010 and 2020
  • The heat season has grown by 46 days since that decade
  • Heat-related deaths in the US increased by more than 50% between 2000 and 2025
